title: Classes, objects, constructors and sort()
overview: Module 3 introduces object-oriented basics: a class groups related data, a constructor fills it, `this->` separates fields from parameters, and heap objects are used with `->`. It also shows why a function must not return the address of a local object, and practises `sort()` and a few judge problems.

concepts.explain: A class is a blueprint; an object is one filled-in copy of it.
concepts.snippet: class Student { public: int roll; double gpa; };

concepts.explain: A function with the class's name that runs when the object is created and sets its fields.
`this` points to the current object; `this->x` means the field `x`.
`new Student(...)` returns a pointer; use `p->field` to reach fields.
Return by value (a copy) or return a heap pointer; never return `&local`.

files.title: Your first class and object
files.what: Defines a `Student` class with `name`, `roll` and `gpa`, creates one object and fills it field by field.
steps: `class Student { public: ... };` describes what every student has.
`a.roll = 13; a.gpa = 4.5;` set fields with the dot operator.
A char-array name can't be assigned with `=`, so `strcpy(a.name, temp)` copies it.

check.a: `name` is a char array, and arrays can't be assigned with `=` in C/C++.

files.title: Filling objects from input
files.what: Reads the fields of two `Student` objects straight from `cin`.
steps: `cin >> a.name >> a.roll >> a.gpa;` fills `a` (name is one word).
files.input_note: Two lines: name roll gpa (name without spaces).
files.output_note: `Rahim 11 3.75` and `Karima 12 4` - note `4.0` is printed as `4` because `cout` drops trailing zeros.

check.a: By default `cout` prints doubles without trailing zeros; use `fixed << setprecision(2)` to keep them.

files.title: Object fields with spaces in the name
files.what: Uses `cin.getline` for names with spaces and `cin.ignore()` to skip the newline left after the numbers.
files.input_note: Name line, then `roll gpa` line, twice.
files.output_note: `Sakib Ahmed 10 4.56` and `Nabil Hasan 12 4.54` - the full names were kept.

check.a: An empty string, because `getline` would read the leftover newline.

files.title: Constructors
files.what: A constructor is a special function with the class name that fills the object at the moment it is created.
steps: `Student(int r, int c, double g)` copies the arguments into `roll`, `cls`, `gpa`.
Read `r c g` from input and build `karim(r, c, g)` the same way.
files.input_note: roll class gpa for the second student.
files.output_note: `21 7 3.8` for `rahim` (fixed in code) and `33 9 4.25` for `karim` (from input).

check.q: Does a constructor have a return type?
check.a: No, not even `void`; its name is the class name.

files.title: this-> when names clash
files.what: When constructor parameters have the same names as the fields, `this->roll = roll;` tells them apart.
steps: `this` is a pointer to the object being built.
`this->roll` is the field; plain `roll` is the parameter.
Two objects are made and printed.

check.q: What would `roll = roll;` do inside the constructor?
check.a: Assign the parameter to itself; the field stays uninitialised.

files.title: Dynamic object with new and ->
files.what: Creates one object on the stack and one on the heap; heap objects are used through a pointer with `->`.
steps: `Student rahim(45, 8, 3.3);` is a stack object - use `.`.
`Student* karim = new Student(1, 8, 5.0);` is a heap object.

files.title: Returning an object by value
files.what: A function can return a whole object; the caller gets a copy, so it is safe even though the original was local.
files.output_note: Prints `254.95` - that is `2`, `5` and `4.95` glued together because no spaces were printed between them.
files.watch_out: Add `<< " " <<` between the fields to make the output readable.

check.q: Why is returning the object itself safe while returning its address is not?
check.a: Returning by value copies the data out before the local object dies.

files.title: Why we need dynamic objects (the bug)
files.what: Returns a pointer to a local object; the object dies when the function ends, so the pointer dangles.
steps: After `fun()` returns, that stack memory is gone.
`main` reads through the dead pointer - undefined behaviour.
files.output_note: Prints `0 0 0` here instead of `2 5 4.95`: the memory was reused. Other runs or compilers may print other garbage or crash.
files.watch_out: This file is intentionally wrong - never return the address of a local object.

check.a: Create the object with `new` inside `fun()` (see the next file) or return it by value.

files.title: Why we need dynamic objects (the fix)
files.what: Same idea, but the object is made with `new`, so it lives on the heap after `fun()` returns.
steps: `fun()` does `new Student(2, 5, 4.95)` and returns the pointer.

check.q: Who is responsible for deleting the object here?
check.a: The caller (`main`), since it received the pointer.

files.title: Practice: highest math marks (fields set by hand)
files.what: Makes three students, fills them field by field, and prints the name of the one with the highest math marks.
steps: If rahim beats both others print rahim; else if karim beats both print karim; else print rafiq.
files.output_note: Prints `Rahim` because 96 is the highest mark.
files.watch_out: The task asked for a constructor (see `practice_problem1_2.cpp`), and ties at the top fall into the `else` and print the wrong student.

check.q: With marks 96, 96, 90, what does this code print?
check.a: `Rafiq` - neither of the tied students is strictly greater than both others, so the `else` runs.

files.title: Practice: highest math marks with a constructor
files.what: Same task, now with a constructor that takes all five fields and `this->`.
steps: The constructor copies the name with `strcpy(this->name, name)` and assigns the rest.
Three objects are built in one line each.
The same comparison chooses the winner.
files.output_note: Prints `Rahim` (99 is the highest). The build shows warnings, not errors.
files.watch_out: Passing `"Rahim"` to a `char*` parameter triggers a warning in modern C++; use `const char*`.

check.q: How do you silence the "string constant to char*" warning?
check.a: Declare the parameter as `const char* name`.

files.title: Practice: copying a dynamic object
files.what: Builds a heap `Cricketer` named `dhoni`, copies its fields into a new heap object `kohli`, deletes `dhoni`, and prints `kohli`.
steps: `kohli = new Cricketer;` and copy each field (`strcpy` for the country).
`delete dhoni;` - kohli still has its own copy.
Print kohli's data and delete it.
files.output_note: `The jersey number of Kohli is 7 and he is from India` - the data survived deleting dhoni.

check.q: Why is `kohli = dhoni;` (pointer assignment) wrong here?
check.a: Both pointers would point to the same object; after `delete dhoni` kohli would dangle.

files.title: Sorting with sort() and greater<int>()
files.what: Sorts an array in ascending order with `sort(a, a+n)` and in descending order with `sort(a, a+n, greater<int>())`.
steps: `sort(a, a + n)` sorts from index 0 up to (not including) n.
files.input_note: First line n, then n numbers.
files.output_note: Three lines: the original `3 9 1 7 4`, ascending `1 3 4 7 9`, descending `9 7 4 3 1`.

check.q: Why is the end argument `a + n` and not `a + n - 1`?
check.a: `sort` takes a half-open range: it stops just before the end pointer.

files.title: Comparison
files.what: Reads `A S B` and checks whether the sign matches the real relation between the numbers.
steps: Print Right if (`<` and a<b) or (`>` and a>b) or (`=` and a==b).
files.input_note: `A S B` with spaces, S is `<`, `>` or `=`.
files.output_note: Input `3 = 3` prints `RIght` - notice the capital I.
files.watch_out: The `=` branch prints `RIght` (typo) and would be judged wrong. It should be `Right`.

check.q: Why does `cin >> a >> s >> b` work for `5 > 4`?
check.a: `cin` skips spaces and reads one non-space character into the `char`.

files.title: Mathematical Expression
files.what: Reads `A S B = C`; prints Yes if the expression is true, otherwise the correct result.
steps: Read `a s b q c` (q is the `=` sign).
If the computed value for the sign equals `c`, print Yes.
files.output_note: Prints `42`, the correct answer, because 6*7 is not 40.

files.title: Palindrome Array (two pointers)
files.what: Compares `a[i]` with its mirror `a[n-i-1]` for the first half of the array.
steps: For `i` in `0..n/2-1`, if `a[i] != a[n-i-1]` set false and stop.
files.input_note: First line N, then N numbers.
files.output_note: `4 7 1 7 4` reads the same both ways, so `YES`.

check.q: Why does the loop only go to `n/2`?
check.a: Each check covers a pair; past the middle you would compare the same pairs again.

files.title: Smallest Pair in one pass
files.what: Minimises `A[i] + A[j] + j - i` with i < j. Rewrite as `(A[i] - i) + (A[j] + j)` and keep the best `A[i] - i` seen so far.
steps: For each test read `N` and the array.
`min_ai_minus_i` holds the smallest `a[i] - i` among indices before `j`.
For every `j > 0`, try `min_ai_minus_i + a[j] + j` as the answer.
files.complexity: Time O(n) per test · Space O(1) extra
files.input_note: T tests; each has N and then N numbers.
files.output_note: Test 1 (`20 1 9 4`) gives `7` (pair 1 and 4). Test 2 (`-5 2 -1`) gives `-4` from -5 + -1 + 2.

check.q: Why update `min_ai_minus_i` after using it for index `j`?
check.a: Because i must be strictly less than j; updating first would allow i = j.

files.title: Sorting with sort()
files.what: Reads N numbers and prints them in ascending order using `sort`.
files.input_note: First line N, then N numbers.

check.q: What would you pass to `sort` to get descending order?

recap: Use `.` for objects and `->` for pointers to objects.
Constructors set fields at creation time; `this->` resolves same-name clashes.
Returning `&local` gives a dangling pointer; use `new` or return by value.
Copying heap objects means copying their fields, not their pointers.
`sort` works on a half-open range `[a, a+n)`.

check_yourself.q: What is the difference between `Student s(1,2,3.0);` and `Student* p = new Student(1,2,3.0);`?
check_yourself.a: The first is a stack object that dies at the end of its scope; the second lives on the heap until `delete p`.

check_yourself.q: Inside a constructor with parameter `gpa`, how do you set the field `gpa`?
How do you sort an int array `a` of size `n` in descending order?
